sources.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes (arXiv:1907.09415v6, 2026)
sources.locator: Chapter 3 §§3.1–3.3 (including §3.3.2), PDF pp.35–39 (printed pp.24–26): Simon promise, coset state, Hadamard sampling, rank/recovery discussion and classical lower-bound decision variant. Appendix A.1, PDF p.205: F2^n with entrywise addition.

contents.name: Simon hidden-XOR promise and coset fibers
contents.reason: Section 3.1 states the hidden XOR period and paired fibers; the local definition fixes the total-function search relation and proves nonempty label assignments.

contents.name: Binary coordinate vector space over F2
contents.reason: Appendix A.1 identifies entrywise F2 arithmetic; the local item verifies all coordinate vector-space axioms and the standard basis, including n=0.

contents.name: One-query Simon state and target measurement
contents.reason: The Simon procedure evaluates one coherent oracle query and measures the output; the local algorithm gives ordered registers, a valid instrument, gate count, and discarded outcome.

contents.name: Coset-pair conditional state and computational Born weights
contents.reason: The source derives the two-address conditional state; the local proof verifies instrument validity, branch traces, normalization, and the exact computational-basis Born-weight lemma.

contents.name: Trace formula for a computational-basis Born weight
contents.reason: The source uses computational-basis measurement probabilities; the carrier derives the squared-amplitude rule from the local trace and Dirac interfaces.

contents.name: Hadamard amplitudes and annihilator sampling
contents.reason: The source expands the two Hadamard terms and obtains orthogonality to the hidden string; the local proof computes every amplitude and invokes its explicit annihilator basis.

contents.name: Explicit F2 Gaussian row reduction
contents.reason: The source identifies Gaussian elimination modulo two; the local algorithm specifies pivots, free-variable choice, failure, and n=1 behavior.

contents.name: Rank rise and finite-prefix expected sampling
contents.reason: The source gives the subspace-size rank-rise calculation and expected-query summary; the local proof establishes exact probabilities and finite-prefix truncated expectations.

contents.name: Budgeted quantum recovery and bit accounting
contents.reason: The source motivates repeated sampling; the local items prove Gaussian recovery, a finite failure cap, the termination tail, expected queries, and charged bit work.

contents.name: Finite random injection distribution on nonzero masks
contents.reason: The source lower-bound discussion motivates a uniform mask distribution; the local definition normalizes the injection family and verifies its promise exactly.

contents.name: Classical randomized collision lower bound for the decision variant
contents.reason: Section 3.3.2 proves a distributional decision lower bound; the local item gives a complete posterior and collision argument for search on the nonzero-mask promise.

contents.name: Classical randomized birthday-collision upper bound
contents.reason: The assigned QA04 scope requires Simon quantum recovery and the classical lower bound; it makes no matching classical collision-search upper-bound claim.

contents.name: Exercise 7.13 perfect-success amplification
contents.reason: The source references this improvement only as an exercise without a proof; the local carrier instead proves its own bounded-failure cap completely.

contents.name: Finite rank and sampling instances
contents.reason: The source motivates repeated independent samples; the companion checks n=1 and n=2 branches, rank, elimination, and cap failure by finite calculation.

sources.title: Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms (17 April 2025)
sources.locator: Chapter 6 §6.1, PDF pp.33–37: the finite-abelian HSP and Simon's order-two subgroup/coset sampling context. Chapter 5 §5.3, PDF pp.29–32: deterministic adversarial HSP lower-bound comparison.

contents.name: Simon as the order-two subgroup problem over F2^n
contents.reason: Chapter 6 identifies Simon's subgroup {0,s} in F2^n; the local definition fixes the nonzero-mask search relation and total oracle widths.

contents.name: Finite-abelian coset states and annihilator Fourier sampling
contents.reason: The HSP treatment independently cross-checks coset-state sampling; all specialized F2 amplitudes and normalizations are proved locally.

contents.name: Coordinate annihilator and rank recovery
contents.reason: The source describes orthogonality constraints; the local proof supplies an explicit coordinate basis and dimension, including the n=1 boundary.

contents.name: Deterministic adversarial HSP query lower bound
contents.reason: Section 5.3 treats a deterministic adversarial HSP model, not the randomized nonzero-mask Simon search distribution proved in this item.

contents.name: One-query coset-state algorithm context
contents.reason: The general HSP notes corroborate the query/coset-state convention; the local algorithm specifies the exact registers, instrument, and query/gate counts.

sources.title: John Preskill, Quantum Information, Chapter 6: Quantum Algorithms (updated November 2020)
sources.locator: §6.1, PDF pp.11–13: Simon promise, output measurement, coset-pair state, Hadamard amplitudes and rank equations. §6.5, PDF pp.27–33: general HSP and coset-state Fourier-sampling context.

contents.name: Simon nonzero XOR-period promise
contents.reason: Section 6.1 states the two-to-one XOR-period promise; the local definition also handles m≥n−1 and proves a promised function exists.

contents.name: Measured two-preimage state and branch weights
contents.reason: The source derives the conditional pair state; the local proof supplies a complete finite-instrument trace calculation and exact branch law.

contents.name: Computational-basis Born weight identity
contents.reason: The source gives the basis-measurement probabilities in Simon's circuit; the local lemma proves the squared-amplitude trace formula directly.

contents.name: Uniform orthogonal equations and annihilator basis
contents.reason: The source obtains y·s=0 equations; the local proof gives the explicit n−1 dimensional solution basis and the finite cardinality.

contents.name: Hadamard sample law and rank growth
contents.reason: The source derives uniform samples satisfying y·s=0; the local proof computes amplitudes, Born weights, and normalization.

contents.name: Classical-query collision comparison
contents.reason: Section 6.1 presents a classical collision argument; the local item proves the exact randomized search lower bound under its own finite distribution.

contents.name: Claim that n independent samples lie in s-perp
contents.reason: The source says n independent y vectors can be sampled, but every y is orthogonal to nonzero s so s-perp has dimension n−1; this impossible count is unused and corrected locally.

contents.name: General hidden-subgroup and Fourier-sampling setting
contents.reason: Section 6.5 provides general HSP context; the local process states its finite independent-sample law and imports no general abelian-HSP theorem.

contents.name: Finite n=1 and n=2 Simon examples
contents.reason: The companion's boundary calculations are verified directly from its finite oracle table and local sample/recovery results.
